analysis:
Documentation-only PR. Changes: docs/developer/test.md (date bump; new head lines 177-210 documenting opt-in live test ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests; Related list lines 505-508) and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (date bump; new table row at head line 119 describing provider-staged destinations built from zeroed host bytes, skipping eval/stream fences so staging avoids MLX evalLock, with up to one destination of staging scratch charged in the import plan). No source code is changed in the supplied units, so no concrete regression is observable.

Security-relevant observations for later passes (T-041 cache/timing oracle, T-028 residual GPU memory, TB-007): the ssd-kv-cache.md row describes a behavioral code change in the SSD restore path (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift). Those sources were not supplied, so the claims are unverified: that zeroed host-source destinations are fully overwritten by authenticated restored data, that the staging scratch charge bounds memory, and that the evalLock-independent restore timing does not widen the cross-tenant TTFT oracle (restore latency now less coupled to other tenants' prefill). The documented test uses an isolated ephemeral cache, a clean env (env -i) and an explicit output path, and runs with a listed-variable allowlist, so it adds no attack surface. The test's 1s contention check is a regression guard. I recommend reviewing the code that accompanies this doc change against T-041 if it is part of the same PR. The missing source is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
